archetypes.name: bash-python-parity
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds symmetric changes to both the Bash live path (ship-pr.sh) and the Python migration tree (ci_monitor.py); asymmetries in defer conditions, predicate definitions, or upfront-log reuse logic are a primary failure mode the plan explicitly calls out.
archetypes.prompt_body: For every new behavioral gate the plan introduces — blind-rerun skip on deterministic default, upfront log ready-only reuse, fix-loop defer for logs-in-progress / error / jobs-in-progress, and the substantive-attempt predicate — verify the plan specifies the matching behavior in BOTH the Bash tree (scripts/ship-pr.sh run_evaluate_failure) and the Python tree (python/ci_monitor.py evaluate_failure). Look for asymmetries where a plan step names one implementation but not the other, uses different state names or condition orderings between trees, or lists test cases for one side with no parity test on the other. Check that the rc values (gh_logs_rc==3 / logs.state=='in_progress', rc not 0 and not 3 / logs.state=='error', ci_failed_rc==3 / jobs_state=='in_progress') map 1-to-1 across both trees with identical defer semantics. Flag any plan sentence that resolves a finding for Bash but defers the Python equivalent to 'parity' without specifying the exact change. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: predicate-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan defines a multi-condition predicate for code_fix_attempted_on_ready_log with explicit carve-outs; gaps or ambiguous cases in the predicate definition are the direct path to mis-routing exhaustion to the wrong exit code.
archetypes.prompt_body: Enumerate every combination of (gh_logs_rc / logs.state) × (ci_failed_rc / jobs_state) × (fix machinery entry point) the plan describes and verify the predicate definition covers all of them without gaps, overlaps, or underspecified branches. Specifically check: what the plan says happens when gh_logs_rc==0 and ci_failed_rc is some value other than 0 or 3 (not mentioned in the edge-cases section); whether the vendor_rc==4 branch and the per-job verification-retry branch are the only two ways to set the flag or whether additional fix-machinery paths in the existing script could set it without the plan accounting for them; and whether the 'do not set the flag when' carve-out list is exhaustive given the actual branching structure in ship-pr.sh around lines 2622-2693. Also verify the plan's predicate description in the main text, the FINDING_1 resolution, and the 'Substantive code-fix attempt predicate' section are mutually consistent — no sentence in one block should contradict another. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: exit-contract-sync
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a new ci-fix-exhausted exit-3 bail reason that touches ship-pr.sh, ship-pr.md, SKILL.md, ci-decide.md, and multiple test files; incomplete propagation across any of these surfaces leaves a broken or undocumented contract.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the new ci-fix-exhausted bail reason across every surface the plan touches: needs_user_bail_reason and is_autonomous_exit3_bail_reason extensions in ship-pr.sh, the ship-pr.md documentation update, the SKILL.md Step 8+ Exit 3 sub-procedure trigger extension, the ci-decide.md disambiguation section, and the test assertions in test-ship-pr.sh and test-implement-step8-exit3-first-fixer.sh. For each surface, verify the plan specifies the exact change needed — not just 'update' or 'extend' but the specific value, flag, or sentence to add. Check whether the plan handles the reverse: any test that currently asserts exit 3 only for first-fixer-non-health needs updating to also accept ci-fix-exhausted, and any test that must NOT fire ci-fix-exhausted (launcher-only, rebase-storm) must assert exit 4 explicitly. Verify the plan's distinction between BAIL_NEEDS_USER_INPUT=false for ci-fix-exhausted and BAIL_NEEDS_USER_INPUT=true for ci-decide's fix-attempts-exhausted is consistently reflected in every updated file's plan description. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
